incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api p99 spike > 6s, queue length rising rapidly in us-east. Auto-remediation attempted and failed. See runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/hosted-queue
megan (oncall-sre): I'm on it. /ack. Creating incident channel and paging eng-runtime + autoscale.
sam (eng-runtime): looking. Metrics: us-east gpu-util=99.8%, queued_requests=~120k, enqueue_rate=3.4k/s, p50=120ms p95=2.1s p99=6.8s
lee (autoscale): autoscaler reports hitting configured max_nodes=48 for gpu pool (policy:prod-us-east). Provisioner attempts returning cloud error: "INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA: GPUs requested exceed quota". Rate of instance creation is 0.0/s
toni (product-support): Customer-facing: several high-tier customers seeing 504s and timeouts. Support queue filling. Notified CS leads.
megan (oncall-sre): quick mitigation options — (1) per-tenant emergency shedding (2) route heavy tenants to fallback region (3) enable degraded model variant for all hosted traffic. Thoughts?
sam (eng-runtime): we can flip a model variant via traffic-policy but model load time ~2-3m. Degraded variant: rtx-gpu-quant-small -> halves token throughput but lowers latency and memory pressure.
lee (autoscale): we can also raise max_nodes, but quota change takes hours. Manual spot request will also fail due to quota. Not an immediate option.
devops (cloud): tried manual node creation, cloud returns: "QuotaExceeded: You have 0 available GPU quota in us-east-1 for type a100". Filing urgent quota request but ETA unknown.
toni (product-support): ETA for customers? Support needs a mitigation we can tell customers to expect degraded throughput for next 30-45m.
customer-success: top impacted customers (anonymized): cust-23, cust-9, cust-77. All high qps. They are calling support.
eng-platform: we have a 'spill-to-region' routing flag on the traffic-router. Command to toggle (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://router.internal/redwood/v1/policy -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' -d '{"route":"spill","from":"us-east","to":"eu-west","selector":"qps>200"}'
```
eng-platform: if we enable that, heavy tenants will land in eu-west where capacity exists. Expect additional network RTT ~80-150ms but should reduce local gpu saturation.
megan (oncall-sre): proceed with spill. eng-platform, please enable and confirm.
eng-platform: enabling flag now.
eng-platform: :white_check_mark: flag enabled. Routing change pushed.
megan (oncall-sre): applying degraded path for general traffic as well (enable quantized-small fallback). Command:
```
POST /admin/traffic/override
{"fallback_model":"gpt-quant-small","apply_to":"hosted-default","duration_min":60}
```
sam (eng-runtime): fallback enabled. Starting model spin-up across nodes in eu-west and warm caches.
megan (oncall-sre): immediate effect visible: queued_requests dropped from 120k -> 55k over 10m. p99 down from 6.8s -> 3.1s. p95 ~1.4s. Still elevated but stable.
toni (product-support): relaying to customers: "We've enabled temporary degraded routing and model fallback to reduce timeouts. Expect improved success rate; small increase in latency for requests routed cross-region."
devops (cloud): quota request acknowledged by cloud, but approval ETA 2-4 hours. Not helpful for immediate.
lee (autoscale): leaving autoscaler max unchanged. We'll monitor queue slope. If growth resumes, next step is selective tenant throttling (rate-limit heavy API keys) — need list from CS.
customer-success: sending tenant list now.
megan (oncall-sre): ok, applying per-tenant emergency throttle for the top 5 heavy keys to 30% of normal QPS. Command executed.
megan (oncall-sre): queue now 38k, p99 2.7s. Success rate improving. :thumbsup:
eng-platform: capturing rollout config and timestamps for postmortem.
sam (eng-runtime): note — we saw KV cache pressure on runtime; the quantized model reduces KV usage which helped reduce memory eviction churn.
toni (product-support): opening incident severity notification to customers with status updates every 15m.
megan (oncall-sre): preparing handoff. I'm on call for another 10m. Summary for next oncall (@raj):
- incident: hosted-api ue-south (us-east) GPU pool exhausted -> autoscaler blocked by cloud quota. Root cause: burst traffic from marketing campaign + no spare capacity
- actions taken: enabled cross-region spill to eu-west, enabled degraded model fallback (gpt-quant-small), applied per-tenant emergency throttles for top 5 keys
- current state: queue 38k and trending down, p99 2.7s, affected customers mitigated via fallback/route. Cloud quota pending.
- follow-ups: increase pool slack for prod, add autoscaler fallback to try warm spare regions earlier, add guardrail for per-tenant qps spikes, review marketing burst pre-warning process.
raj (next-oncall): taking over. Acknowledge and will monitor. Please post latest dashboards and any lingering manual flags status.
megan (oncall-sre): flags: spill-to-region=enabled, fallback-model=enabled, emergency-throttles=applied. Dashboards: https://go/redwood/dash/hosted-queue
raj (next-oncall): thanks. I'll keep the channel open and coordinate postmortem. If queue growth resumes, I'll escalate to infra leads to open capacity request. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident channel created and severity updated to SEV2. Handoff recorded at 1765131600."
